newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-WEAH LOOKING FOR REVENGE AS AFRICAN CUP BEGINS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAH LOOKING FOR REVENGE AS AFRICAN CUP BEGINS.

text.p: George Weah leads a large contingent of African professionals back to the continent this weekend for the start of the qualifiers for the 1998 African Nations' Cup finals.
The AC Milan striker and his Liberian teammates have been assembling in neighbouring Ivory Coast for his team's trip to Kinshasa for their group six match against Zaire on Sunday.

The match, which is one of 14 qualifying games to be played throughout Africa this weekend, is a chance for Weah to settle a score against the Zairian team which denied Liberia a place in the quarter-finals of the last Nations' Cup finals in South Afrca.
Liberia's team will rely heavily on their European-based legion against a Zairian team, whose coach Muntumbile Santos has also called up a host of his players from European clubs.

Algeria play their first match since their defeat by Kenya in the World Cup qualifiers in June and caretaker coach Hamid Zouba is hoping three French-based expatriots will enhance his career prospects against the Ivory Coast in Algiers on Friday.

Zouba, whose predecessor Ali Fergani was banned from coaching in Algeria for life after Kenya knocked the country out of the World Cup qualifiers, has called up Moussa Saib and Abdelhafid Tasfaout from French champions Auxerre for the group two match.

Algeria are also expected to give a first cap to Abder Rahmane of French club Le Havre. Rahmane was the hero of unfashionable Nimes' progess to the French cup final last season and their qualification for this season's European Cup Winners' Cup beforehis move to Le Havre.
The Ivorians, in turn, are considering a return to the team of former Bordeaux winger Youssouf Traore, who has been playing in Saudi Arabia.
Another African soccer hero, Bruce Grobbelaar, will be playing and coaching Zimbabwe in their group one match against Sudan in Khartoum on Saturday.
Grobbelaar has called up five foreign-based players for the team but will have to do without fellow English-based professional Peter Ndlovu, who is injured.
Other missing high profile players will be Ghana's captain Abedi Pele and the Mozambican goalkeeper Rui Evora.
Abedi Pele has turned down a call-up by coach Sam Arday for Saturday's home match in group one against Angola to concentrate on building up his fitness at new Bundesliga club 1860 Munich.

The three-time African Footballer of the Year said in a radio interview this week that he still needed time to "get back into my normal shape and I've pleaded with Ghana to leave me out of this match".
Rui Evora, the captain of his country, will be missing when Mozambique travel to Lusaka to meet Zambia in group seven after being sent off during the last Nations' Cup finals in January.
He has to sit out the opening match of the 1998 qualifiers, leaving the Mambas threadbare in defence for a difficult away assignment.
